- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Bronchitis is an inflammation of the bronchial tubes, with two main types: acute and chronic.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common symptoms of acute bronchitis include coughing, chest congestion, fatigue, mild fever, shortness of breath, sore throat, headaches, muscle aches, and loss of appetite.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Common symptoms of chronic bronchitis include persistent coughing with mucus production, shortness of breath, chest tightness, fatigue, recurring respiratory infections, and blue-tinged lips or fingers in severe cases.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The user should consult with their primary care physician if experiencing a persistent cough.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] General tips to manage a cough include staying hydrated, using a humidifier, taking over-the-counter medications, getting plenty of rest, and avoiding irritants.

- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Expectorants work by increasing mucus production, thinning out thick mucus, breaking down mucus, and clearing mucus from airways.
